speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of pain during urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever accompanying the current knee swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle followed by knee), urethritis (painful urination), and a history of inconsistent condom use in a young male is classic for Reactive Arthritis. Given the sexual history and joint symptoms, I need to rule out Gonorrhea as a cause of septic arthritis or urethritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Gram stain & culture, and Synovial fluid analysis from the right knee. REQUEST TEST: Chlamydia DNA PCR and Gonorrhea NAAT.
